Marks a stated row total or activity share, which spans every material rather than naming one.

The recycling obligation table ends each producer group with a Total row. Mapped to All, like the stated row totals elsewhere, so a sum over material_canonical never double counts it. row_kind marks it as Total.
An activity share, published as a percentage. It must never be summed into a tonnage.
A count of registered producers, not a tonnage.

Materials sit in columns 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of the sheet; column 3 is an empty spacer. Every value is read by its column position against its own table's header row, so a material with no figure leaves a gap rather than shifting the ones after it.

The activity shares are the apportionment the regulations fix for who carries the obligation on a given tonne: 6 per cent raw material manufacturing, 9 per cent conversion, 37 per cent pack/filling and 48 per cent selling. They are published as percentages against each activity row and are identical in both years. The import tables use a different split again — 6, 15 and 52 per cent across conversion, pack/filling and selling — which does not sum to 100 and is published that way.

The total recycling obligation was 7,939,063 tonnes for registration year 2023 and 7,901,506 for 2024, a fall of 0.5 per cent. Each is the sum of a general obligation and a material specific one: 481,302 plus 7,457,761 for 2023, and 615,066 plus 7,286,440 for 2024. The general share more than doubled between the two years while the total barely moved.

Producers carrying an obligation fell from 6,968 in 2023 to 6,941 in 2024, and allocation producers from 230 to 193. The published strings also give the split between direct registrants and scheme members — 362 direct of 6,968 in 2023, 318 of 6,941 in 2024 — and are kept whole in value_as_published, since only the leading count is parsed to a number.

There is no 2025 file. This dataset covers registration years 2023 and 2024 only, because the PRN producer obligation regime was replaced by pEPR. For the obligation on the new basis, see the pEPR dataset, which publishes a 2026 obligation of 7,590,797 tonnes — 3.9 per cent below the 2024 figure here. The two are calculated on different bases and the comparison is indicative, not like for like.
